Say I have 4 bytes to work with. So I can express at most 1111111111111111, or 65,535 in decimal.

Is there any way to get it so 4 bytes could express 70,000 unique numbers?
Is it impossible for the number of values in a range to be greater than the number of values in a domain?

For the range to be larger than the domain would require that one value in the domain map to multiple values in the range. So you would no longer have a function.

However, you can extend your range if you're willing to have holes in it. So while 4 bytes can't express 70k unique numbers, if you used a floating-point format you could express numbers ranging from well above that to easily that far into the negatives. You'd just lose precision so some numbers that have a difference of one or two would seem to be equal.
